title: Same envelope-shape bug fixed for certificate verify is still live in handleSignatureVerify in the same component
claim: The C15 fix rebuilds the envelope from `.meta` + `.data` only in handleCertificateVerify. handleSignatureVerify (line 194) still does `setSignatureResult(response.data as SignatureVerifyResponse)`, and the backend's POST /v1/signatures/verify returns the identical sibling-envelope shape `{ success, valid, data: { hash, signatureAlgorithm } }` (apps/backend/routes/api/integration/interoperability.js:252-259). apiClient unwraps `.data` and harvests `valid` into `.meta` (api-client.ts:451-455), so `signatureResult.valid` is undefined and the public trust portal renders every VALID signature as failed with hash '-'. Pre-existing on main, not introduced here, but it is the exact defect class the branch just proved real on the same public surface — needs a follow-up fix using the same meta+data rebuild. (handleTraceLoad at line 225 has the same stale cast, but /v1/trace/events requires a partner API key so the public portal 401s there regardless.)

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds — refutation fails at every link of the chain:

1. Backend shape confirmed: POST /v1/signatures/verify (apps/backend/routes/api/integration/interoperability.js:228-259) has NO auth middleware (unlike /v1/trust/registry and /v1/trace/events which use requirePartnerApiKey), so the public portal reaches it, and it returns exactly the sibling-envelope shape `{ success: true, valid, data: { hash, signatureAlgorithm } }` (lines 252-259).

2. No reshaping in between: apps/web-app has no /api/interoperability route handler; /api/* goes through the passthrough proxy app/api/[...path]/route.ts which streams request.body and the response body untouched. next.config.ts rewrites only /uploads/*.

3. apiClient unwrap confirmed (api-client.ts:75, 451-456): success branch returns `data: body.data ?? body` → the inner `{ hash, signatureAlgorithm }` — and `valid` is not in ENVELOPE_RESERVED_KEYS (`success/data/error/message/code`), so extractEnvelopeMeta harvests it into `.meta`, not `.data`.

4. Component confirmed (trust-verifier-portal.tsx:194): `setSignatureResult(response.data as SignatureVerifyResponse)` stores only `{ hash, signatureAlgorithm }`, while SignatureVerifyResponse (types/interoperability.ts:54-61) expects `{ valid?, data?: { hash, signatureAlgorithm } }`.

5. Render confirmed (trust-verifier-portal.tsx:410-414): `signatureResult.valid` is undefined → a VALID signature renders `c.signature.fail` in red; `signatureResult.data?.hash` is undefined → hash renders '-'. Only the algorithm line survives by accident via the `|| 'RSA-SHA256'` fallback.

6. The C15 fix (lines 102-113) rebuilds meta+data only in handleCertificateVerify; handleSignatureVerify still carries the stale pre-fix cast and even the stale comment claiming the cast restores the full shape. The parenthetical about handleTraceLoad also checks out: same stale cast at line 225, but /v1/trace/events/:entityType/:entityId requires a partner API key (interoperability.js:474), so the public portal 401s there.

The only existing test (trust-verifier-portal-copy.test.tsx) is a copy test and does not exercise envelope shape, so no test run settles this differently — the static chain is complete and unambiguous. The failure scenario concretely holds on this code: every VALID signature on the public trust portal renders as failed with hash '-'.

title: Client-level 30s default widens blast radius beyond the three stated hops — audit-chain lock hold and money txs included
claim: Verified no transaction relies on the short 5s default for correctness (the only explicit-option call sites are the checkout settle and the new onsite decision, both already 30s), so the change is safe as such. Two blast-radius consequences worth recording: (1) auditLogger.logWithin serializes all same-org audit writers on pg_advisory_xact_lock held until the caller's tx ends (middleware/audit-logger.js:590-606) — a wedged interactive tx can now stall every audit-logged action in that org for up to 30s instead of 5s, and maxWait 10s makes waiters queue rather than fail fast, so worst-case head-of-line blocking rises ~6x under contention; (2) the new default also applies to every money-path interactive tx (invoice, refund, journal-entry, payment-closure), i.e. behavior change beyond the three hops named in the comment — in the safe direction (fewer spurious aborts) and tier-check classifies the diff TIER=B (probe run on this diff, path-based), but the operator should see this stated explicitly in the merge summary rather than discover it later.

verdict.reasoning: The finding's failure scenario holds concretely on this code. (1) prisma-database.js:90-102 sets client-level transactionOptions { timeout: 30000, maxWait: 10000 } on the single shared PrismaClient, replacing Prisma's 5000/2000ms defaults for every interactive tx. (2) audit-logger.js:590-606 confirms logWithin acquires pg_advisory_xact_lock(AUDIT_CHAIN_LOCK_NS, hashtext(orgId)) through the CALLER's tx, and the code comment itself states the lock is held until the caller's tx commits/aborts — so a wedged tx now pins the per-org audit chain for up to 30s instead of 5s (~6x head-of-line blocking), and log() at line 505 uses a bare $transaction (no options) contending on the same cluster-wide lock, so all audit-logged actions in the org are affected. (3) Grep confirms the only production call sites with explicit options are checkout-settlement-service.js:254 and audit-onsite-service.js:939-940 (both 30000ms), exactly as the finding claims; every money-path tx (invoice-service.js:429, refund-service.js:351, manual-journal-entry-service.js:402, period-close-service.js:253, credit/debit-note, payment-slip x4) is a bare $transaction that silently inherits 30s — behavior change beyond the three hops named in the comment at prisma-database.js:81-89. The only imprecision is minor: maxWait bounds pool/tx-slot acquisition, not advisory-lock waits (those are bounded by the waiter's own 30s timeout), but under contention the pool saturates and new callers do wait 10s vs 2s before failing, so the queuing claim is substantively right. The finding is accurate, correctly scoped as minor/advisory (safe direction, TIER=B), and its ask — state the widened blast radius explicitly in the merge summary — is grounded.

title: startedAt:null dead-ends re-entry into a COMPLETED inspection (GpsVerificationLog model does not exist in this schema)
claim: GpsVerificationLog has no Prisma model anywhere in apps/backend/prisma/schema/ (only FarmAuditChecklistItem and FarmAuditPhoto exist in audit-onsite-evidence.prisma), so on the current deployment _resolveStartedAt's guard `typeof prisma?.gpsVerificationLog?.findFirst !== 'function'` is ALWAYS true and BOTH context routes now return startedAt:null for every audit — including COMPLETED ones — and startInspection's create is equally skipped so no marker is ever persisted. verdict.reasoning:
Verified each link of the failure scenario on the working tree (fix/phase0-walk2-endline):

1. No Prisma model: grep for `GpsVerificationLog`/`gps_verification` across all `**/*.prisma` files in the repo returns zero matches (only jest mocks in __tests__ provide the model). So on the real generated client `prisma.gpsVerificationLog` is undefined, the guard at apps/backend/routes/api/audit/onsite.js:96 is always taken, and BOTH context routes (onsite.js:279 and :380) return startedAt:null for every audit. startInspection's create is equally guard-skipped (audit-onsite-service.js:474), so no start marker is ever persisted — null forever.

2. Regression vs before: `git diff main...HEAD -- onsite.js` confirms both routes previously returned `audit.createdAt` (always truthy for an existing row), which sent the client straight to the checklist stage with savedAnswers seeded.

3. COMPLETED status: submitDecision flips AuditChecklist.status to 'COMPLETED' for PASS/FAIL (audit-onsite-service.js:893).

4. Entry still renders: page.tsx:511-527 gates the "เริ่มตรวจประเมินภาคสนาม" link only on `queueItem?.inspectionMode === 'ONSITE'` — no status check — linking to /provider/audits/{application.id}/inspect.

5. Context loads (does not 404) for a COMPLETED audit: the FE calls `/audit/onsite/application/:applicationId/context` (audit-service.ts:413), whose resolver falls back to the most-recent row of ANY status when no IN_PROGRESS row exists (onsite-audit-resolver.js:37-42). 6. Dead end: client-view.tsx:128 `setStage(res.data.startedAt ? 'checklist' : 'start')` — stage depends solely on startedAt; savedAnswers are seeded into state but never shown on the start stage. The StartScreen's only affordances (เริ่มตรวจ and the DM-4 farm-coords fallback) both funnel through startWithFix → POST /start (client-view.tsx:209-311). startInspection then runs `_ensureAuditStatusEligible(audit, ['IN_PROGRESS'])` (audit-onsite-service.js:463; the helper at :371-384 throws AUDIT_STATUS_INVALID for anything else) → route maps to 409 (onsite.js:483) → red toast "เริ่มตรวจไม่สำเร็จ", stage stays 'start'. The in-diff comment discusses only the every-reload start-screen cost for live audits, not the COMPLETED dead end. Running the route jest suite would not settle this — its mock prisma provides gpsVerificationLog, i.e. it exercises the provisioned path, not the deployed schema. The finding concretely holds; severity minor (read-only re-entry UX regression, no data loss) is fair.

title: Client-default tx timeout silently changes every money-path transaction; tier-check's path net classifies it B

No money computation, fee amount, settlement equation, webhook verification, or invoice logic changed, and the direction mirrors the operator-blessed SETTLEMENT remedy (F-SETTLE-TX-LOST); but the failure envelope of money txs changes: a wedged refund/invoice tx now holds row locks up to 30s (vs 5s) before forced rollback and queues 10s (vs 2s) for a pool slot, changing contention behavior under load. scripts/probes/tier-check.sh (run in-session on the diff file list) returns TIER=B because prisma-database.js's PATH carries no money keyword — a shared-infra file reaching money-path runtime behavior is exactly the 'plausibly touches a Tier-C surface' case the probe's C-inclusive philosophy wants surfaced.
